messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: S1 — anomalous session 'ghosting' observed on edge-proxy cluster eu-west-1. Multiple clients showing rapid session reuse from different IPs. Paging @oncall. Thread started 4829007777
oncall: I'm on it. initial checks: any signs of data exfil or leaked tokens?
maria: quick snapshot of metrics — 5xx rate stable, but auth-401 -> 200 replay pattern from ~120 distinct IPs. Session IDs reused across accounts. seen in proxy logs: `session_id` present in requests from unrelated client IPs.
shaun: adding logs: sample lines show same session_id header but different geos. suspicious. also noticed a streaming log-forwarder recently restarted in staging last night — possible leak path.
sec-sre: important — assume tokens compromised until proven otherwise. Containment checklist: 1) throttle/block suspicious CIDRs 2) revoke active session tokens / rotate service keys 3) snapshot affected hosts 4) preserve logs for forensics. I'll coordinate key rotation.
dan: agreed. raising emergency key rotation for the edge service account. plan: create new service key in KMS, update edge proxy secrets in vault, perform rolling restart of proxy group (canary then full). ETA for canary push ~10m after key creation.
liza: I'll open a support bridge and draft a customer impact note. need scope: which customers saw session reuse? maria can you run query to map session_id -> customer_id?
maria: running quick query now (kusto):
```
proxy_logs
| where timestamp > ago(30m)
| where session_id in (external_replay_list)
| summarize count() by customer_id, session_id, client_ip
| order by count_ desc
```
results show 8 customer_ids with >10 hits each, majority are internal test accounts but 2 production customers touched.
oncall: blocklist deployed for top 25 CIDRs (temporary) :white_check_mark: traffic to blocked IPs dropped 87% of replay events. still seeing some via CDN edge nodes.
shaun: isolating suspected log-forwarder instance (staging-shipper-03) and snapshotting disk. grabbing process list and outbound connections.
sec-sre: rotation plan for service tokens: 1) provision new KMS key 2) create new service principal creds 3) publish to vault path `secret/edge/prod` 4) rolling restart with health checks and canary 5) revoke old creds after 2 successful canaries. I'll run the KMS step now.
dan: KMS key created `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/edge-rot-4829/cryptoKeys/rot-1`. starting vault write to `secret/edge/prod` with new creds.
maria: cross-checking logs for any S3 put/forwarder spikes: none in last 24h to external buckets. there was a small batch push to internal staging-bucket at 02:13 that matches timestamp of log-forwarder restart. investigating contents.
liza: support bridge up (zoom link) and templated note ready. recommend notifying the two affected customers with limited details and that we're rotating keys and blocking suspicious traffic. legal looped in.
sec-sre: old service key scheduled for revoke in 15m, will only flip after we confirm canary stability. please avoid pushing unrelated deploys.
oncall: canary with new creds started at 4829009800. health checks passing. no auth regressions.
shaun: snapshot uploaded to forensics bucket, marking as read-only. process dump attached to the artifact.
maria: final tally: replay events dropped by 94% after CIDR blocks + key canary. remaining ~6% attributed to legacy CDN caches — invalidation in progress.
sec-sre: revoking old key now. revocation done :lock: old creds invalid. will keep watch for 1 hour then close incident if no resurgence.
liza: customer notices sent to affected accounts with mitigation summary.
dan: thumbs — followup action items: review log-forwarder auth flows, add stricter egress rules, create a canary for logshipper restarts.
incident-bot: Incident update: S1 -> mitigated, monitoring. timeline recorded. closing pager at 4829010945 :memo:
